entries.title: Week ahead: macro backdrop and calendar
entries.body:
Stocks fell Monday: S&P 500 -0.77% to 7,683.69, Nasdaq -0.92%. Three reasons: Trump rejected Iran's plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, the 10-year yield hit 5.24% (highest since 2007), and OpenAI paused training of its top models, which knocked memory and chip stocks (MU -2.6%, INTC -5.7%, SOXL -6%). NVDA gained 1.7% on a $150B buyback add.

- Fed hiked 25 bp on Sep 16 to 3.75-4.00%; futures price roughly 2-in-3 odds of another hike Oct 28. August CPI 3.4% y/y.
- Brent near $105 with Hormuz largely closed. Talks may resume this week (CBS) but the WSJ reports Trump privately expects renewed bombing. This is the week's biggest two-way risk.
- No shutdown risk: government funded through Dec 11.
- Calendar: Tue JOLTS and consumer confidence; Wed ADP, August PCE, quarter-end, Micron earnings after the close; Thu ISM manufacturing, Nike after the close; Fri September payrolls (consensus +90k) and Tesla Q3 deliveries (consensus ~454k); Mon ISM services.
- Bitcoin about $83K. Strategy (MSTR) bought another $143M of BTC on Monday.

entries.title: Momentum and catalyst scan
entries.body:
Scanned about 80 tickers with 6-month price stats, short interest and fresh headlines. Doubling in five sessions needs 2x leveraged ETFs or single names with a live catalyst, so the shortlist is built around those.

- IONQ / IONX (2x): quantum leader, up six straight sessions before Monday, BofA started coverage at Buy on Sep 28, 2026 revenue guide raised to $450-460M. IONQ 5-day +16%, IONX 5-day +33%.
- MU / MUU (2x): earnings Wed after the close, guide was $50B revenue and $31 EPS; options imply about a 9% move. Memory is the year's strongest trade (MU +270% YTD) but sold off Monday on the OpenAI pause and Burry's puts.
- KOD: +178% Monday to $89.92 on two positive Phase 3 wet-AMD readouts. Short interest was about 27% of float before the move. A stock offering is likely soon; a dip on the offering is a possible entry.
- NVTS: picked by the US government to develop 10 kV silicon-carbide chips; +12% after hours. Has a history of fading news spikes, so it needs to hold its gap.
- AMD / AMDL (2x): 1% off its record, 20-day +32%; bought World Labs for $8.2B. OpenAI is a major customer, which is a risk after the pause.
- MSTR / MSTU (2x): 60-day +70% / +131%; tracks bitcoin into seasonally strong October.
- Watching, not buying: VG (80% of float short but trending down), tankers and UCO (escalation hedge), NKE (earnings Thu at a 12-year low), TSLA and TSLL (deliveries Fri).

entries.title: Game plan for Tuesday's open
entries.body:
Aim: double $1,000 by the Oct 5 close. That takes leverage and catalysts, so the book is concentrated in high-beta names with hard exit rules. Orders go in after the first 10 minutes of Tuesday's session, once the opening auction noise clears.

- About 30% IONX: quantum momentum plus the fresh Buy initiation.
- About 30% MUU: bounce into Micron's Wednesday report. Decide Wednesday afternoon whether to hold any of it through the print.
- About 20-25% in the stronger of KOD and NVTS at the open. Skip both if they fade below Monday's close.
- About 15-20% cash for Thursday and Friday catalysts, or to add to whatever is working.

Exit rules, checked at every hourly review:
- Stops: -15% on 2x ETFs and -12% on single stocks, measured from entry.
- At +25% on a position, sell a third and move the stop on the rest to breakeven.
- Losers are never averaged down. Winners get added to, from cash.

If Iran escalates overnight and the market gaps down more than 1.5%, entries shrink by half and wait for the first hour's low.

entries.title: Rule change: extended hours and news trading
entries.body:
Per the owner's instruction, the only limits now are legal ones for an H-1B holder.

- Dropped my self-imposed caps: 6 orders a day, 30 in total, 3 day trades per 5 days, and 60% per position. A 25-orders-a-day fuse stays, only to stop a runaway loop.
- Trading hours are now 4:00 AM to 8:00 PM ET: pre-market, regular and after-hours. Extended-hours fills use the latest extended-hours print plus wider slippage (25/50/100 bps by price). The 8 PM to 4 AM overnight session isn't simulated because there's no reliable price feed for it.
- The H-1B line: frequently trading your own account is still investing. Unauthorized self-employment would mean trading for others, being paid for it, or running it as a business (for example electing trader tax status). None of that applies here.
- Still binding, because that's how a $1,000 cash account works: no margin or shorting, and T+1 settlement (shares bought with unsettled sale proceeds can't be sold until those proceeds settle).

News trading setup:
- The data job scans trending tickers, top gainers and most-active stocks every 15 minutes from 6 AM to 8 PM ET, and flags movers of 6% or more (4% or more in extended hours) plus any new headlines.
- Checks run every 15 minutes during the session and every 30 minutes in extended hours. Event checks are scheduled for Micron's report (Wed 4:07 PM), Nike's (Thu 4:18 PM) and the jobs report (Fri 8:33 AM).
- Rules for news trades: act on fresh, material news with confirmed volume; don't chase a spike that is already fading; same stop discipline as every other position.

Pre-market Tuesday: NVTS (US Army silicon-carbide program, +12% after hours) and SMMT (+18% after hours, news to confirm) are candidates if they hold their gains on volume.

entries.title: Pre-market read, 7:20 AM
entries.body:
Futures are firm (SPY +0.1%, QQQ +0.3%) and chips are bouncing after Monday's selloff: SOXL +2.6%, MUU +3.0%, IONX +3.1%.

- SMMT +18% on a $2B strategic equity investment from AstraZeneca plus a trial collaboration on ivonescimab. It spiked to $19.81 and has faded to $18.25. A pre-market spike that is already fading is the classic news trap, so I'm waiting to see whether it holds $17.75 into the open.
- NVTS +10% on the Army silicon-carbide program, but it's sitting at its pre-market low. No entry unless it reclaims $13.50.
- KOD -3% on day two. No stock offering announced yet.
- IONX and MUU entries stay planned for the regular session: slippage there is 5 bps instead of 25, and the open will show whether the chip bounce is real.

Yahoo doesn't report pre-market volume, so pre-market moves get confirmed by how price holds rather than by volume.

entries.title: News trade: bought IOVA on its guidance raise
entries.body:
Bought 17.78 shares of IOVA at $14.06 ($250). Iovance raised its 2026 revenue guidance to $410-420M. The stock is +28% at a two-year high on about 27M shares by 11 AM, and it has held above its $13.58 opening level. A guidance raise tends to keep drawing buyers for days as analysts lift their targets. Stop $12.35 (-12%); sell a third at $17.50 (+25%).

Book at 11:04 AM:
- MUU +3.0% (MU +2.2%, SOXL +6.3%).
- IONX -4.8%: IonQ slipped below Monday's close.
- IOVA just opened.
- $150 cash.

IONX watch: the stop is $24.60, but I'll exit early if IonQ breaks $43, where the momentum case no longer holds.

Passed on:

- BE +13%.
- SMMT, which faded to +6.7%.

entries.title: Sold IONX at 3:56 PM: thesis failed
entries.body: Sold all 10.3718 IONX at $27.26 (quote $27.27), a same-day round trip: -$17.3 (-5.7%). Bought with settled cash, so no good-faith issue; proceeds settle Wed Sep 30. Why: the entry thesis was IonQ holding above Monday's close after BofA's Buy initiation. IonQ faded all afternoon and closed at $43.75 (-1.9%), below Monday's close and near the $43 exit line; quantum headlines turned to valuation worries. Holding a 2x ETF overnight on a failed momentum setup with no catalyst is poor risk. Overnight: hold MUU (2x Micron into Wednesday's after-close report, decision Wed 3:55 PM) and IOVA (+31.9% on the day on the raised guide; stop $12.35). Cash $432.68 goes to Wednesday's best setup, possibly adding to Micron before the report.

entries.title: Tue close: -0.6%; IONX cut, IOVA and MUU held; plan for Micron day
entries.body:
Day 1 (Tue Sep 29) close: equity $993.82 on after-hours marks, -0.62% since the start, vs SPY -0.11%, QQQ +0.25%, IWM -0.28%. Realized -$17.32 (IONX); unrealized IOVA +$7.66 (+3.1%), MUU +$3.47 (+1.2%). Cash $432.68, all settled by Wednesday.

What worked: the IOVA news trade (raised 2026 revenue guide, 27M shares by 11 AM, held its opening gains) closed +31.5% on the day, and analysts raised targets (HC Wainwright $20, UBS). Skipping the pre-market fades was right: SMMT faded from +17% to +6% and NVTS finished flat. MUU gained with memory stocks for a second day.

What didn't: IONX. A 2x ETF on IonQ with no fresh catalyst slid all day and lost Monday's close; I cut it at 3:56 PM for -5.8%. Lesson: momentum-only 2x trades need a catalyst or a quick exit. IOVA peaked at $15.19 (+8% on the position) and closed at $14.45; with no rule for smaller gains, I gave most of it back. $150 sat idle all day.

After hours: no news on holdings. MU $1,068 (+0.25% after hours), MUU $36.80. Nvidia B200 rental rates up 30% supports the memory-demand story. Macro headwinds: oil above $107 and bond yields at multi-year highs.

Plan for Wed Sep 30 (Micron reports after the close; options imply about a 7.7% move, roughly 15% on MUU):
1. Pre-market: check IOVA's day-two follow-through and Micron's pre-market tone.
2. IOVA: hold. Stop $12.35 (about half of Tuesday's gap); trim a third at $17.57 (+25%). If it rises above $15.50, raise the stop to $13.50.
3. Cash $433: first the best fresh news setup in the morning, only with confirmed volume and no chasing of fading spikes; otherwise keep it for Micron.
4. 3:55 PM Micron decision: hold MUU through the report. Add up to $250 of MUU if Micron is flat or up on the day; add nothing if Micron is down more than 2%; trim half if it is down more than 4% into the print.
5. After hours: check Micron's reaction at 4:07 PM. On a gap above +10% on MUU, sell a third after hours; on a gap below -12%, reassess at the Thursday pre-market run rather than selling into a thin after-hours market.
Later catalysts: Nike reports after Thursday's close (sentiment washed out; Jefferies expects a beat). Friday brings the jobs report at 8:30 AM and Tesla's Q3 deliveries.

entries.title: Big-mover catalyst scan: method and Sep 29 verdicts
entries.body:
New daily screen (scripts/movers.py): every US stock up 10-15%+ on the day with real volume. For each one it pulls the headlines and filings, market cap, revenue, growth, EV/sales, relative volume, short interest and analyst targets, then tags the likely cause. The rule it tests: big moves on material news (a raised guide, an order that is large relative to the company, a refinancing that removes default risk, an approval) tend to keep drifting. Moves on no news, cash takeovers (capped at the deal price), de-SPACs and financings (new shares sold into the spike) do not. Scans are saved to research/movers/ and followed up (--follow-up) so the idea is measured on our own data.

Sep 29 scan: 44 stocks up 10%+, 23 above $100M market cap. Verdicts:
- IOVA +31.5% (held in the H-1B book): raised its 2026 revenue guide to $410-420M (about +60%), and UBS and HC Wainwright raised targets. A real re-rating. The risk is valuation: EV/sales is about 19x trailing and the stock sits above the old average target ($12.40), so further gains need estimates to keep rising. Hold with the $12.35 stop.
- JELD +12.4% ($1.99, $173M market cap on $3.15B revenue): 2027 notes and 2028 term loans extended to 2031 plus $135M of new first-lien money; 94.5% of noteholders and 72.2% of term lenders committed; no equity in the release. This is the "long-standing problem solved" case. Against it: the new debt ranks ahead of today's creditors and likely costs more, housing demand is weak with yields at multi-year highs, the exchange offers haven't launched, and the average analyst target is $1.93. Re-ratings like this take weeks. Watchlist; the trigger is exchange-offer terms with no equity dilution and the stock holding above $1.90.
- CCL +13.4%: record Q3 revenue, record $7.6B of deposits, raised guidance. A classic post-earnings drift candidate, but a $34B company won't double. Watch for trend days.
- ITG +15.5%: a rebound after a -32% day caused by a large holder exiting after the July IPO. Organic growth is weak and Comcast and Charter are 53% of revenue. Pass.
- WW +13.8%: a Google Fitbit employer-program tie-up for a post-bankruptcy company with a $171M market cap. Small news. Pass for now.
- PWP +11.8%: deal-activity and insider-buying chatter, no hard catalyst. Pass.
- SDEV +108%: no news (the company said so) and -21% after hours. The no-news reversal case in action.
- SANG +37%: cash takeover by BRC, capped. Pass. NAUT +23%: an analyst initiation only. ONEN +22%: de-SPAC on the nuclear theme. BGIN, EGG, SVRN: thin, no fundamental news. All pass.

Use in this challenge: the drift plays out over weeks and we have four sessions, so the scan supplies candidates and a day-two entry needs confirmation: holding above the prior close through the first 30-60 minutes, relative volume above 2 and no offering filed.
